newsitem.title: JAPAN: MBOMA LETS HIROSHIMA END GAMBA'S UNBEATEN RUN 2-0.
newsitem.headline: MBOMA LETS HIROSHIMA END GAMBA'S UNBEATEN RUN 2-0.

text.p: Osaka Gamba star Patrick Mboma lost concentration and allowed Hiroshima to end Gamba's remarkable early season winning run in the J.League with a 2-0 victory on Wednesday.
The Cameroonian forward, who had led Gamba's winning streak this season, failed to clear after trying to control with his chest a free kick by Hiroshima's Noh Jung Yoon three minutes into the game.
Australian forward Graham James Arnold snatched up the resulting loose ball and made an easy tap-in goal.
Hiroshima went two-up in the 35th minute when forward Takuya Takagi headed home a perfect cross from fellow Japanese international Hiroshige Yanagimoto.
Mboma, who scored four goals and set up five more in Gamba's opening three games, also let slip several clear scoring chances as Gamba's three-match winning streak came to an end.
But Gamba stays top of the table on goal difference after four games in the first-stage competition ahead of second-place Kashima Antlers.
Antlers remained the only unbeaten team in the league with a game in hand after dealing Yokohama Flugels their first defeat of the season.
Fullback Akira Narahashi netted the 65th-minute winner in a previously goalless game, taking the Antlers to a 1-0 win before a capacity home crowd of 15,000.
Goals by Brazilian forward Mabilia and Masashi Nakayama bounced Jubilo Iwata back from Saturday's home loss to Cerezo Osaka with a 2-1 away victory over newcomers Vissel Kobe.

Cerezo, which caused an early-season sensation together with hometown rival Gamba, added a point with a 5-4 penalty shoot-out win over visiting Kashiwa after the two teams failed to break a 2-2 deadlock in extra time.
Hiratsuka notched a 1-0 home win over Ichihara with a strike in the 86th minute by recently signed Brazilian Lopes, two-time top scorer in the second-tier Japan Football League.
Two goals by national team forward Shoji Jo guided Yokohama Marinos to a 3-1 win over Kyoto at home, while Urawa routed winless host Fukuoka 3-0 and Shimizu beat Kawasaki 2-1 at home in extra time.
